ports.note: Takes a table and gives back the same table with fewer rows. Key columns, value field and unit are unchanged, because selecting rows does not change what the table measures.

ontology.note: No ontology mapping yet. The receipt names the column, the values kept, how many rows were kept and dropped, and any named value the table did not hold.

changes.description: On the standard Inspector and configuration dialog (experiment 186). The panel holds the step's name, its input, one sentence saying what it keeps, Configure…, a one-line result after a run (rows kept and left out, and any value named that the table does not hold), the Manual, Evidence and Version links, and Duplicate and Remove. The column, the values or the range are in the dialog, which shows how many rows they keep, and the table, before they are applied; a selection that keeps nothing is refused there. Nothing is written until Apply. What the step stores is unchanged, so saved workflows open as they were.

evidence.note: Unit tested on the same Table IX fixture, including the ordering the named values impose and a value absent from the table. Nothing here establishes that a selection is an honest one: keeping a subset of categories is exactly how a figure can mislead, and the widget cannot tell a partition from a cherry-pick. The range is unit tested (tests/select-a-range.test.mjs) and built from an empty canvas through the dialog in tests/select-range.browser.mjs, Chromium.
